findings.title: Expired join timeout leaves remaining flusher processes un-terminated
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes.items()` checks `remaining_time = deadline - time.time()` and executes `break` if `remaining_time <= 0` before calling `process.terminate()`. When a timeout is passed to `join(timeout)`, `self.next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting on the first process in the loop can consume the entire timeout budget. The `break` then exits the loop immediately, leaving all subsequent child processes in `self.processes` running instead of terminating them. Instead of breaking out of the loop when the deadline has passed, the loop should skip waiting and still call `process.terminate()` on every remaining `multiprocessing.Process`.

findings.title: Zeroassigned shards causes ZeroDivisionError when max_processes is set
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` evaluates to `0` when `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty and `max_processes` is `None` (or `0`), making `self.num_processes = 0`. Even if `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` is 0, the loop doesn't run, which is fine; however, if `max_processes` is passed as `<= 0` (e.g. `--flusher-processes 0`) while `buffer.assigned_shards` is non-empty, `self.num_processes` becomes `0` (or negative) and `i % self.num_processes` on line 65 raises `ZeroDivisionError` (or `KeyError` for negative modulo). `max_processes` / `--flusher-processes` should be validated to be at least 1.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name `shards` vs `shard`
findings.body: Lines 185 and 195 emit `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` with `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, whereas line 199 emits `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural). Using two different tag keys (`shard` vs `shards`) for the same `shard_tag` value across sibling flusher metrics makes dashboarding and grouping by shard inconsistent.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched at the start of the test
findings.body: Line 15 of `test_basic` patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` on line 62 (with comment `# Give flusher threads time to process after drift change`) does not actually sleep at all and provides no synchronization.
